newsitem.title: USA: Hilton to make selective changes in gaming.
newsitem.headline: Hilton to make selective changes in gaming.

text.p: Following shareholder approval of Hilton Hotel Corp's merger with Bally Entertainment Corp, top executives from both companies said Thursday they plan few changes to gaming operations.
In one change, Bally's Atlantic City hotel called The Grand will likely be remaned as a Hilton hotel, executives said at a news conference following Hilton's shareholders meeting here.
The companies are already exploring changing signs at The Grand, Arthur Goldberg, newly named president of Hilton's gaming operations, said.
In Las Vegas, most of the changes will come through consolidation of property management functions such as single-point printing, data processing, employment and training.
The companies will not revise development plans for Bally's new hotel on the Las Vagas strip being built on a theme around Paris.
"We love that theme," Hilton Chief Executive Stephen Bollenbach said. "It doesn't need anything in the way of expansion or change so we plan to go forward with that."
In New Orleans, where both Hilton and Bally operate casinos the companies have decided not to pursue a management contract for a permanent land-based casino there.
Bollenbach said the company had discussed a management agreeemnt with Harrah's Jazz, an affiliate of Harrah's Entertainment Inc, but those talks have ended.

By November or December, Hilton expects to have completed the acquisition of Bally, and Goldberg said he expects to have the gambling operations of the two companies running together smoothly at closing.
Hilton's acquisitions and deals will not end with the Bally deal. Hilton continues to plan acquiring major hotel operations, and Bollenbach said there are currently "substantive" talks in that area.
He declined to name companies he was looking at.
On the gaming side, any acquisitions are not likely to occur until after the Bally deal is completed.

After that, however, Bollenbach said any takeover targets must have a strong cash flow. He said the company would more likely acquire specific properties as opposed to making an acquisition solely to have a presence in a market.
Finally, the company might boost its stake in Ladbroke Group Plc after making an initial five percent investment in January next year, as previously announced.
Hilton can raise its stake to 20 percent without notifying the company. "That is a target of opportunity and will depend on price, quite frankly, Bollenbach said.
